title: Surgical Admin cli-let and Replayable Simulation Runbooks
creator: Nina Patel
description: Create a lightweight, surgical 'cli-let' binary and a replayable simulation layer for runbooks that lets oncall/operators execute gated remediation steps in dry-run and live modes. The focus is idempotent primitives, strong auditability (integrated with audit-events service), and a lightweight simulation harness to rehearse incidents against sanitized traces.
acceptance_criteria: cli-let exposes a minimal set of idempotent primitives (drain-node, restart-service, adjust-route, cache-evict) with RBAC checks
Each executed step emits structured audit events to /audit/events and attaches a runbook_run_id
Simulation mode can ingest a sanitized trace and produce deterministic dry-run logs without mutating production resources
Runbook executions can be recorded and replayed in the sandbox environment with preserved timings and KV cache state snapshots
Console shows per-step telemetry: wall_time, success/failure, error class, and tokenized operator comments
Automated safety gates prevent escalations for P0 incidents unless two approvers confirm in the tool
infra_changes: Adds small SQS queue for replay scheduling, DynamoDB table runbook_runs (sharded by org), and a new audit-events consumer to attach runbook metadata. Requires IAM role for cli-let to write to audit stream and read KMS-protected snapshot objects.
decisions: Chose event-sourcing for runbook_runs instead of full snapshotting to keep storage minimal and enable streaming replays
Sanitized trace format will be a compressed newline-delimited JSON (ndjson.gz) to balance readability and size
Simulation harness will run in a dedicated sandbox namespace rather than relying on ephemeral prod namespaces to reduce blast radius
Opted to reuse existing audit-events service for traceability rather than adding a bespoke datastore to reduce integration overhead
